content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "missing_justification", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quote appears verbatim and, in context, is the text's own admission that the lower-bound claim for its construction (n pieces of 2d, one of d) is still to be proved. The text establishes only the parity/cancellation invariance f=(n+1)d under the restricted hypothesis that Xiang splits each 2d piece into exactly two parts; other allocations are handled only by two n=2 numerical examples (\"split one big into 3\", \"uses only 1 cut\") and the vague remark \"We argued they give Liu at least as much... Need to prove best response for Xiang... is indeed to split each big once.\" No all-n argument covering arbitrary distributions of the n cuts appears anywhere. Moreover the targeted value (n+1)/(2n+1) is not the correct c_n = 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) (n=2: 0.6 vs 4/7), so the construction itself is wrong. The lower-bound obligation is unmet."}
